newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Thomson gives Lithuania's Hermis BB- for long-term.
newsitem.headline: Thomson gives Lithuania's Hermis BB- for long-term.

text.p: Thomson BankWatch said on Friday that it had assigned Lithuania's Hermis Bank a long-term senior debt rating of BB- and a short-term local currency debt rating of LC-2.
Thomson said in a statement that the BB- rating was equivalent to the sovereign ceiling. It is the first rating assigned to Hermis Bank by an international rating agency.
Thomson said that the ratings reflected Hermis' emergence as one of the strongest players on Lithuania's banking scene, which is recovering from a crisis which erupted at the end of 1995.
"It (Hermis) continues to benefit from the uncertainty in Lithuania's banking system as depositors and borrowers take flight to quality," the statement said.
Hermis, the second largest private bank in Lithuania, had a profit of 8.6 million litas in the first half of 1996.
The bank is 76 percent foreign owned. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) owns a 25 percent equity stake in the bank.
Its shareholders decided earlier this week to boost the bank's share capital by 23 million litas, to 90 million litas from 67 million litas.
While noting that Hermis' "non-performing loans are high", Thomson said that "the level compares well with most banks in Lithuania".
"Its (Hermis') underlying profitability ratios remain strong and for 1996 its expected ROAA should be the highest in Lithuania," Thomson said.

"This rating (LC-2)...reflects Hermis' overall satisfactory financial condition and its management's prudence as well as our belief that it will continue to develop as a major commercial bank in the market," Thomson's Ramin Habibi was quoted as saying in the statement.
"In addition, we believe Hermis' supportive shareholder, the EBRD, will further assist in strengthening corporate governance," Habibi added.
Thomson assigned leading Lithuanian bank Vilniaus Bank a BB- long-term local currency debt rating and a short-term local currency debt rating of LC-1, the highest, last October.
